short: PURA and PURB (Pur-alpha and Pur-beta) are PUR-repeat proteins that bind purine-rich DNA and RNA, with a strong preference for single strands rather than duplex. The PUR element was defined as a repeated purine-rich sequence upstream of the human c-MYC P1 promoter, at a site of DNA bending inside a replication initiation zone, and was given the consensus GGNNGAGGGAGARRRR. The PUR repeats fold into a Whirly-like domain, and Pur-alpha can unwind double-stranded DNA rather than simply read it. These proteins act mostly as repressors, best characterized on the smooth muscle alpha-actin promoter, where they bind the GGN-repeat strand of core enhancer elements. De novo PURA variants cause PURA syndrome, a neurodevelopmental disorder with neonatal hypotonia, seizures and severe developmental delay.
long:
## The factors

Three PUR-repeat genes exist in humans: PURA (Pur-alpha), PURB (Pur-beta) and the less studied
PURG. PURA and PURB are broadly expressed, with PURA especially abundant in brain. The proteins are
built from tandem PUR repeats; crystallography of Pur-alpha showed that two repeats pack together
into a single Whirly-like domain, a fold otherwise associated with plant single-stranded
nucleic-acid-binding proteins, presenting an unusual continuous binding surface rather than the
discrete base-reading elements of a zinc finger or helix-turn-helix. A third repeat mediates
dimerization between molecules. This architecture explains the central functional fact about the
family: PUR proteins are not conventional double-stranded sequence-specific transcription factors.
They bind purine-rich single-stranded DNA and RNA with high affinity, and Pur-alpha can actively
unwind duplex DNA rather than reading it intact. Pur-alpha also binds RNA, including
trinucleotide-repeat transcripts, and localizes to stress granules, so its functions extend beyond
transcription into RNA handling and, in the original work, into DNA replication.

## The motif

The literature element comes from mapping a site of DNA bending 1.6 kb upstream of the human c-MYC
P1 start site, near the center of a reported replication initiation zone. Methylation interference
mapped specific guanosine contacts in a 24-mer, and the derived consensus was GGNNGAGGGAGARRRR, a
sixteen-base purine-rich element found at replication origins and in gene flanking regions from
yeast to human. In practice the element is usually described more loosely as a GGN repeat, and
binding is strand-selective: the purine-rich strand is bound, the complementary
pyrimidine-rich strand is not. There is no half-site grammar, no spacing rule, and no palindrome.
The data here disagree with this, and the disagreement is worth stating plainly. This family
contains exactly one motif, the HOCOMOCO model PURB.H14CORE.0.B.B, whose consensus is ACCCAC, six
bases and only 7.6 bits of information. Its reverse complement, GTGGGT, is GT-rich rather than
purine-rich in the GGN sense, it is far shorter than the published PUR element, its evidence code
B marks it as imported from another collection rather than derived from HOCOMOCO's own ChIP-seq or
SELEX data, and its nearest neighbours across all four databases lie outside this family (best
cross-family similarity 0.73, label agreement 0). There is no PURA motif in these databases at all,
and with a single member the family has no internal cohesion to measure. The honest position is
that the published PUR element is a single-strand, purine-rich sequence that a position-weight
matrix over double-stranded DNA is the wrong tool for, and that the one matrix available under this
key should not be treated as a validated model of PUR binding.

## Where it acts

Documented PUR-protein sites are promoter-proximal and, in the original work, at replication
origins. The best-characterized regulatory target is the mouse and human smooth muscle alpha-actin
promoter, where Pur-alpha and Pur-beta bind the GGN-repeat-containing strands of several cis
elements within a core enhancer and repress transcription. Knockdown showed Pur-beta to be the
dominant repressor in fibroblasts, with the combined action of both proteins needed for full
repression, and the two proteins had indistinguishable binding affinity and specificity in vitro
but distinct protein-interaction profiles, which is how cell-type-specific behavior arises from a
shared site. PUR proteins also occur at the c-MYC upstream region where the element was found, and
Pur-alpha associates with RNA and with cytoplasmic granules in neurons, so not all of its binding
is chromatin-associated.

## Biology and disease

Pura-null mice are viable at birth but develop severe neurological abnormalities with arrested
postnatal brain development and impaired proliferation of neuronal and hematopoietic precursors.
In humans, de novo PURA variants and 5q31.3 microdeletions that remove PURA cause PURA syndrome:
profound neonatal hypotonia, feeding difficulty, seizures or seizure-like movements, and severe
developmental delay with little or no speech. Genotype-phenotype studies across dozens of affected
individuals place missense changes in the PUR repeats among the more severe alleles, consistent
with loss of nucleic-acid binding. PURB has no established monogenic disease association.

## Reading a hit

Do not read a hit under this key as evidence of PUR binding. The only matrix available is a
six-base, 7.6-bit model that does not resemble the published purine-rich PUR element and whose
closest relatives in the motif databases belong to other families. More fundamentally, PUR proteins
prefer single-stranded purine-rich DNA and can unwind duplex, so scanning double-stranded genomic
sequence with a PWM is not a test of PUR binding even in principle. If you care about PUR proteins
at a locus, the useful evidence is a long GGN-rich or polypurine tract on one strand, ideally at a
site with known single-strand character, plus direct biochemical or crosslinking data. Treat any
automated PURB annotation in a scan result as a placeholder.
caveats: This is the weakest family in the atlas. It contains one motif, a six-base 7.6-bit HOCOMOCO model for PURB imported from another collection, with no PURA motif and no internal cohesion. That model (ACCCAC) does not match the published purine-rich PUR element, GGNNGAGGGAGARRRR, and its nearest neighbours in all four databases lie in other families. PUR proteins bind single-stranded purine-rich DNA and RNA and can unwind duplex DNA, so a double-stranded PWM scan is not a valid test of their binding. A hit here should be treated as an annotation placeholder, not as evidence that PURA or PURB binds the sequence.
